evidence.quote:
For every $k\geq1$, the truncation map $$\label{bl:lift:successive}
 g_*(\mathcal O_Z/I^{k+1})\longrightarrow g_*(\mathcal O_Z/I^k)$$ is surjective as a map of additive sheaves on $B$. More generally, for all integers $j<d$, the maps $$g_*(I^j/I^{d+1})\longrightarrow g_*(I^j/I^d),
 \qquad
 g_*(I^j/I^d)\longrightarrow g_*(I^j/I^{j+1})$$ are surjective. Each of these surjections is also surjective on sections over every affine open subset of $B$.

exclusions.reason: The lifting maps concern ideal-power quotients on algebraic cover spaces and are justified by projective boundary geometry and Hodge theory. No software lifting contract follows from terminology alone.

evidence.quote: Let $(X,\Delta)$ be a projective log canonical pair of dimension at most four over $\mathbb C$, with effective rational boundary. If $D=K_X+\Delta$ is $\mathbb Q$-Cartier and nef and $\kappa(X,D)\geq0$, then $D$ is semiample. If $\kappa(X,D)=0$, then $D\sim_{\mathbb Q}0$.

A rational Cartier divisor is semiample if a positive Cartier multiple is generated by global sections; its Iitaka dimension is the dimension of the images of all sufficiently divisible nonempty complete systems, with value $-\infty$ if no such system exists.

exclusions.reason: The conclusions assert existence of a generated Cartier multiple. They do not supply a uniform index or an effective search bound.

evidence.quote: Let $X$ be a smooth connected projective complex fourfold. If its canonical divisor $K_X$ is nef and $\kappa(X,K_X)=0$, then $\nu(K_X)\ne2$.

evidence.quote: Let $V$ be normal and projective over $\mathbb C$, and let $C$ be an effective rational boundary. Suppose that $K_V$ and every component of $C$ are individually $\mathbb Q$-Cartier, that $(V,C)$ is lc, and that it is klt outside $\mathop{\mathrm{Supp}}\lfloor C\rfloor$. If a nonzero effective Cartier divisor $G\sim q(K_V+C)$ has support in $\mathop{\mathrm{Supp}}\lfloor C\rfloor$, for a sufficiently divisible positive integer $q$, and $\mathcal O_V(G)|_{G_{\mathrm{red}}}$ is semiample on the whole reduced scheme, then $\kappa(V,K_V+C)>0$.

Assume abundance for projective lc rational pairs of dimension less than $d$. If $(V,C)$ is a projective $\mathbb Q$-factorial dlt pair of dimension $d$ and $A=K_V+C$ is nef, then the actual restricted rational line bundle $A|_P$, where $P=\lfloor C\rfloor$, is semiample. Its restriction to any reduced union of components of $P$ is also semiample.

The divisor $E=(y=0)$ on $Z$ is reduced and Cartier, with ideal $I=(y)=\mathcal O_Z(-E)$. Put $H_Z=\pi^*p^*H$ and $C_{0,Z}=\pi^*p^*C_0$. With compatible canonical divisors one has $$\label{bl:cov:crepant}
 K_Z+E+H_Z+C_{0,Z}=\pi^*(K_P+p^*C).$$ The pair $(Z,E+H_Z+C_{0,Z})$ is lc and is klt off $E+H_Z$. The map $E\to S_P$ induces an equivariant projective morphism $g:E\to B$.

With the normalization above, $$\begin{aligned}
 F_{<0}\mathcal M&=0,&
 F_0\mathcal M&=(\iota,h)_*\omega_R(D_h),
 \label{bl:hod:lowest-source}\\
 F_{<0}\mathcal N&=0,&
 F_0\mathcal N&=R^1h_*\omega_R(D_h).
 \label{bl:hod:lowest-target}
\end{aligned}$$ The equality for $F_0\mathcal N$ identifies it with a subsheaf of $\mathcal N$. It is induced by simple graph residues and the inclusion of the last term of the relative de Rham complex. The latter inclusion commutes with right differentiation in base coordinates.

Let $(W,\Delta_W)$ be a projective lc rational pair and let $(V,\Delta_V)$ be a $\mathbb Q$-factorial dlt log minimal model. Use the log birational model convention in which divisors extracted on $V$ have coefficient one. On a common resolution $\alpha:U\to W$, $\beta:U\to V$, with compatible canonical divisors, $$\alpha^*(K_W+\Delta_W)
   =\beta^*(K_V+\Delta_V)+E,
 \qquad E\geq0,\quad E\text{ is }\beta\text{-exceptional}.
 \label{bl:eq:abundance-model-comparison}$$ Consequently the adjoints have the same section spaces in sufficiently divisible degrees, and hence the same Kodaira dimension.

 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad D\text{ semiample}.$$ If $\kappa(X,D)=0$, then $D\sim_{\mathbb Q}0$.

Let $\mathbf k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. A finite collection of projective varieties over $\mathbf k$, rational divisors, specified Cartier multiples, morphisms, line bundles, sections, and identities between these data can be defined over a countable algebraically closed subfield $\mathbf k_0\subset\mathbf k$. The field $\mathbf k_0$ admits an embedding into $\mathbb C$.*

*For the data considered here, one can include a log resolution and its discrepancy identities in this descent. Log canonicity, and klt singularities outside a specified reduced boundary, then hold after extension from $\mathbf k_0$ to either $\mathbf k$ or $\mathbb C$. For a rational Cartier divisor on a projective variety over $\mathbf k_0$, nefness, Kodaira dimension, and generation of any fixed Cartier multiple are unchanged under algebraically closed field extension.

Let $(X,\Delta)$ be a projective lc rational pair of dimension at most four over an algebraically closed field $\mathbf k$ of characteristic zero. Suppose that $D=K_X+\Delta$ is $\mathbb Q$-Cartier and nef and $\kappa(X,D)\geq0$. Then $D$ is semiample, and if $\kappa(X,D)=0$, then $D\sim_{\mathbb Q}0$.
Let $X$ be a smooth connected projective complex fourfold. If its canonical divisor $K_X$ is nef and $\kappa(X,K_X)=0$, then $\nu(K_X)\ne2$.
